claims.statement: The settle act has four items in a fixed order — `verify.submit`, `settlement.evolution`, `settlement.sessions`, `settlement.todo` — and completing all four advances the phase without spending an event.

The evolution payload is `artifact|summary[|c=<kept>/<screened>[|cls=<kind>:<n>,...]][|sessions=...][|todo=...]`, and the validator refuses a record whose class counts do not add up to `kept + screened`.

`config.set review.evolution.*` validates each key's shape alone while registration validates cross-field completeness — that split is why a pre-registration can look fine and still fail at the settle call.
`review.note` accepts only `lesson|score`; the older `ev` / `c` / `cls` segments are refused, and the batch's settle keys are single-source archived into `review.evolution.*` before the batch closes.
`gates.require_all_green` is data, not code: with it true, a `verify.submit` carrying `all_green=false` sends the batch back to coordinate and clears the settlement keys.
The host contract owns `agent.endingPrefix` and the `agent.summary` keys, so `nextEndsRun` is a host-declared field rather than a mod-invented one.
`nextEndsRun` is false unless the first settle item is `review.note` and retirement is armed; an unarmed batch therefore never pre-closes the host, which is what keeps a standing run resumable.
Upgrades land after a batch settles and start a new run id — old run directories are never migrated or adopted, so a failed load is answered with a new run instead of a compatibility shim.
